newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Germany said to consider role in Natuna project.
newsitem.headline: Germany said to consider role in Natuna project.

text.p: Indonesia's State Secretary Murdiono said on Monday Germany will seriously consider participating in Indonesia's Natuna natural gas project.
He was speaking to reporters after visiting German Chancellor Helmut Kohl held talks with President Suharto.
"Germany will seriously consider participating in the development of the Natuna project," Murdiono said when briefing reporters on the talks.

Indonesia signed an agreement in late 1994 with U.S. oil giant Exxon Corp to explore the Natuna field in the South China Sea. The field is estimated to contain 210 trillion cubic feet (TCF) of gas, of which 45 TCF are thought to be commercially recoverable.
Indonesian Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie told Reuters on Monday that the development of Natuna upstream projects would be tendered soon.
The field is expected to cost an estimated US$40 billion to develop.
